analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: SOGGY START 2 Nov
key_insights: S&P 500 closed -51bps at 7,541 with a $2bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX -139bps at 27,989, R2K -7bps at 2,809, Dow +41bps at 51,983. Volume was 18.773bn shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.499bn.
Momentum factor fell 6.7% while laggards rose 1% as the US 10-year yield (4.91%) and oil (WTI -8%) pressure eased. S&P Equal Weight outperformed the S&P 500 by about 125bps.
Semiconductors (SOX) kept falling after closing below the 200-day moving average on Friday for the first time since June 2025.

The GS floor activity level was 3 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were moderate net sellers, driven by tech. Hedge funds were moderate net buyers, with scattered cover demand in industrials, tech and healthcare, on muted notional.
Large semiconductor sell tickets on the GS desk from Friday persisted into Monday, with a less pronounced sell skew, and met virtually zero demand.
Debt and equity deals funding the AI buildout continue, with the past week a particularly heavy capital-raising stretch. The note raises the question of how easily the market can absorb this supply.
Rotation into consumer-levered areas on lower oil: Discretionary +2%, with AMZN and Internet names benefiting within TMT.

AAPL after the bell was roughly flat. First take was 'solid' with product revenue slightly better and Services revenue and China slightly worse. It returned $28bn to shareholders in the quarter. Focus for the 5pm ET call: new products, gross margin outlook into the December quarter, and December-quarter revenue guide vs consensus of +6% y/y.

Midterms: Democrats are now above 90% to take the House. GIR sees limited immediate market implications. Divided government makes major policy change unlikely. Higher tariffs (about 2pts in the effective tariff rate) and fiscal negotiations around the Dec 11 funding deadline are the bigger risks.

sector_views.rationale: Discretionary rose 2% as oil fell, with rotation into consumer-levered areas. This describes the day's flow, not a formal rating.
SOX kept falling after closing below its 200-day moving average Friday, with large sell tickets and virtually no demand. This describes the day's flow, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: AAPL reported fiscal Q4 after the close on 11/2. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures. First take was 'solid', with product revenue slightly better and Services revenue and China slightly worse. $28bn was returned to shareholders in the quarter.

AAPL December-quarter revenue guide will be judged against consensus of +6% y/y (consensus estimate, not yet guided as of this note). The 5pm ET call was expected to cover new products, gross margin outlook into the December quarter and the revenue guide.
